cve_summary: Buffer overflow in hw/scsi-disk.c in the SCSI subsystem in QEMU before 0.15.2, as used by Xen, might allow local guest users with permission to access the CD-ROM to cause a denial of service (guest crash) via a crafted SAI READ CAPACITY SCSI command.  NOTE: this is only a vulnerability when root has manually modified certain permissions or ACLs.
commit_message:
scsi-disk: lazily allocate bounce buffer

It will not be needed for reads and writes if the HBA provides a sglist.
In addition, this lets scsi-disk refuse commands with an excessive
allocation length, as well as limit memory on usual well-behaved guests.

Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Kevin Wolf <kwolf@redhat.com>
docstring:
Summary: This code fragment defines a structure for handling SCSI disk requests in a system.

Parameters: N/A

Returns: N/A

Logic: The `SCSIDiskReq` structure encapsulates all necessary information for a SCSI disk operation. It includes a `SCSIRequest` object, which likely contains the command details for the SCSI operation. The `sector` and `sector_count` fields are specified in terms of 512-byte blocks, indicating how data is organized on the disk. The `buflen` field represents the length of the buffer for data transfer, while `iov` and `qiov` are used for managing input/output vector operations, facilitating efficient data handling. The `status` field is used to track the outcome of the request, and `acct` is a cookie for block accounting, which may be used for resource management or performance tracking.
